##### Summary

Underwater image enhancement (UIE) research is trending toward heavy models, while lightweight alternatives are judged by parameters and FLOPs: proxies that say little about latency and energy on the edge accelerators underwater IoT platforms deploy. We report an on-device measurement study of shallow-water enhancement, whose per-channel attenuation physics favors compact quantized networks. Depthwise-separable U-Nets (9k-59k parameters) and a 4.3k-parameter curve model are trained on UIEB, quantized to FP16, INT8, and INT4 (palettized) with weight-only post-training quantization, and deployed via Core ML on the CPU, GPU, and Apple Neural Engine (ANE) of an Apple M3 Pro, with per-frame energy from idle-subtracted SoC power counters. The main 28.9k-parameter model at INT8 on the ANE enhances 256 × 256 frames at 945 FPS and 4.7 mJ/frame with no degradation at the reported two-decimal precision relative to FP16, and +3.2 dB PSNR over raw input on a 90-image held-out UIEB split. Across all 36 configurations on this FP16-compute stack, weight-only quantization provides no consistent latency or energy gain; energy is governed by compute-unit choice (3.6× vs. the GPU, 5.5-5.6× vs. the CPU) and network width. A W8A8 variant engages the ANE integer datapath (-18% latency, -28% energy at -0.37 dB), localizing the neutrality to weight-only PTQ rather than to the model or the NPU. A sub-30k-parameter network already saturates the measured quality-cost trade-off.

##### Summary

Underwater images suffer from unique challenges during restoration, due to absorption and scattering of light. It results in significant loss of fine details, color cast, blurriness, and irregular haze. Existing methods struggle to capture the fine details in complex underwater scenarios. To tackle these difficulties, we propose a novel Edge-guided Feature Refinement (EFR) module using channel attention and integrate this in a vision transformer based architecture. It is precisely designed to recover the blurred details. We also used a window based multi head self attention driven encoder-decoder architecture to enhance both local and global details in underwater images and also reduce the computation complexity.

# Energy-Aware Heterogeneous Deployment of Learned Image Codecs

##### Paul, G.; Nicol, R.; Obara, B.; Bhowmik, D.

#### Proceedings - IEEE International Symposium on Circuits and Systems: 2604-2608

#### 2026

* * *

ISSN/ISBN: 0271-4310

DOI: 10.1109/iscas66217.2026.11562627
Accession: 108161610

##### Summary

Learned image compression (LIC) achieves state-of-the-art compression performance, yet practical deployments often overlook latency and energy - critical constraints for on-device pipelines and bandwidth-limited applications such as drones and satellite imaging. We address this gap with a codec-aware heterogeneous deployment partitioned at the codec's natural bottleneck - the quantised latent - and mapped across devices: large analysis/synthesis transforms to the GPU (high parallel throughput), the compact, pipelined hyperprior to the FPGA (low-power dataflow), and entropy coding to the CPU. The system remains bit-exact with the reference codec and integrates directly with pretrained CompressAI models via exported ONNX subgraphs. Across two pretrained codecs and 1,000 test images, the heterogeneous mapping improves encoder runtime by about 10% and reduces encoder energy by 80% on average relative to GPU-only execution. For the decoder, runtime remains within 1% of the GPU while energy decreases by approximately 78%. Overall, it achieves an energy-delay product about 80% lower than GPU-only and 29% lower than FPGA-only, providing a superior latency-energy trade-off for LIC deployment.
